claim_a.claim_text: Histograms of oriented gradients capture the edge structure that is sufficient for accurate human and object detection.
claim_a.evidence_quote: We show experimentally that grids of Histograms of Oriented Gradient (HOG) descriptors significantly outperform existing feature sets for human detection.

claim_b.claim_text: Learned convolutional features substantially outperform handcrafted feature representations such as HOG and DPM on object detection.
claim_b.evidence_quote: Compared to systems based on the more boutique HOG-like features, mAP for HOG-based DPM ... our R-CNN approach gives a substantial improvement (mAP from 33.7% to 53.7%).

rationale: R-CNN directly demonstrates that learned CNN features substantially outperform the handcrafted HOG features that the earlier paper claimed were sufficient. The contradiction reflects the deep-learning era shift.
